source: NCERT Class VIII, Resources and Development, Geography Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. Land Resource
points: **Land** supports natural vegetation, wildlife, human life, transport and industry; only about **30%** of the Earth's surface is land.
**Land use** = how land is used (farming, forests, pasture, settlement, roads); it depends on **relief, soil, climate and population**.
**Land degradation** (deforestation, overgrazing, mining) is a serious problem; conservation via **afforestation, controlled grazing, shelter belts**.

sections.heading: 2. Soil
points: **Soil** = the thin top layer of the earth's crust supporting plant growth; formed by the **weathering of rocks** over long periods.
Factors of soil formation: **parent rock, climate, relief, time, and living organisms (flora/fauna)**.
**Soil erosion** = removal of topsoil by wind/water (worsened by deforestation, overgrazing); leads to loss of fertility.
**Soil conservation:** afforestation, **contour ploughing, terrace farming, shelter belts, mulching**.

sections.heading: 3. Water
points: Only a **tiny fraction** of Earth's water is usable **fresh water**; demand is rising fast.
**Water scarcity** is caused by growing population, over-use, pollution and uneven distribution.
**Conservation:** avoid waste, **rainwater harvesting**, recycling, and checking pollution.

sections.heading: 4. Natural Vegetation and Wildlife
points: **Natural vegetation and wildlife** are part of the **biosphere**; they provide oxygen, food, medicines and maintain ecological balance.
Threats: **deforestation, hunting, pollution, habitat loss**.
**Conservation:** national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, **biosphere reserves**; the **IUCN Red List** identifies threatened species; protection of **endangered species** (tiger, lion, rhino).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Land use depends on relief, soil, climate, population; ~30% of Earth is land.
Soil forms by weathering; factors: parent rock, climate, relief, time, organisms.
Soil conservation: contour ploughing, terrace farming, shelter belts, mulching.
Fresh usable water is very scarce; conserve via rainwater harvesting & recycling.
Wildlife conservation: national parks, sanctuaries, biosphere reserves; IUCN Red List.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Soil forms from the weathering of rocks** over long periods (parent rock is a key factor).
**Contour ploughing / terrace farming / shelter belts** are methods of **soil conservation**.
**Rainwater harvesting** is a key method of **water conservation**.
**Biosphere reserves** protect whole ecosystems; the **IUCN Red List** flags threatened species.
